title: Reasons for Recent Rise in Costs and Measures to Help Singaporeans Cope
what_it_is: Reasons for Recent Rise in Costs and Measures to Help Singaporeans Cope

sections.label: Inflation impact and statutory charges
sections.summary: Questions ask the Ministry's assessment of inflation's impact on 2022 growth and whether it will delay statutory charge increases, and reasons for rising consumer costs and measures to help consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in light of the higher-than-expected inflation rate in November 2021 (a) what is the Ministry’s assessment of the resulting impact on economic growth in 2022; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider working with the other Ministries to delay the increase in various statutory charges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what are the reasons for the recent rise in costs impacting consumers across many areas; and (b) what policies or measures will be put in place to manage the impact of these increases on consumers, especially lower-income households and those whose livelihoods have been impacted by disruptions caused by the current pandemic.

sections.label: Singapore CPI inflation 2021
sections.summary: Singapore's CPI-All Items inflation averaged 2.5% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2021 and rose to 3.8% in November 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In the third quarter of 2021, Singapore's CPI-All Items inflation averaged 2.5% on a year-on-year basis and rose to 3.8% in November 2021.

sections.label: MAS inflation forecasts
sections.summary: MAS Core Inflation could average in the upper half of the 1% to 2% forecast range, while CPI-All Items inflation is projected at 1.5% to 2.5% in 2022, after 2.3% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For the full year, MAS Core Inflation could average within the upper half of the official forecast range of 1% to 2%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: As for CPI-All Items inflation, it is projected to average 1.5% to 2.5% in 2022, following the 2.3% expected for 2021.

sections.label: Real median income growth
sections.summary: Real median income of full-time employed residents grew by 3.8% per annum over the five years cited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In tandem with economic growth, the real median income of full-time employed residents and that is, after accounting for inflation, grew by 3.8% per annum over those five years I have cited earlier.

sections.label: Lower-income real income rise
sections.summary: For lower-income residents at the bottom 20th percentile, real income rose by 4.6% last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For lower-income residents at the bottom 20th percentile, real income rose by a larger 4.6% last year.

sections.label: Food prices Singapore versus global
sections.summary: Global food commodity prices surged about 30% year-on-year between July and November 2021, while Singapore's domestic non-cooked food prices rose 1.6% over the same period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Notably, while global food commodity prices surged by around 30% on a year-on-year basis between July and November 2021 based on the United Nation's Food and Agriculture Organisation's Food Price Index, Singapore's domestic non-cooked food prices saw a far smaller increase of 1.6% over the same period.
